verdict_in_one_line: 11 capabilities are reachable by a job kind in attempts::ROUTES; 1 capability (machine.answer) is registered in KNOWN_WORKER_IDENTITIES and reachable only through a dedicated Core HTTP route, never by a job; no capability in any of the four audited sources is reached by nothing at all.

production_registration_note.why_it_matters_here: A capability in KNOWN_WORKER_IDENTITIES is not automatically registered. Executor::open_routes registers only what the launch declares (plus text.extract), and the capability surface lists exactly the registered routes. So 'registered + healthy' is a statement about one launch, and a name in the identity list is not evidence of registration.

the_three_declaration_paths.role: the only route-declaring entry point; reads launch.text_worker.routes

the desktop host declares no routes at all; only {python, script, staging}

production_registration_note.consequence: In a staged-runtime or desktop launch, machine.answer is not a registered capability at all: the capability surface would not list it, and POST /api/v1/machine/answers would answer 503 with the executor's own words, 'no worker is registered for machine.answer' (executor.rs:143). It becomes registered only when a launch declares it, which today only the two test contracts (crates/archeaxis-api/tests/contract_machine_answer.rs:29 and contract_machine_retest.rs:33) and the probe scripts/probes/colearning_real_model_smoke.py:138 do.
production_registration_note.capability_surface_cannot_express_this: crates/archeaxis-api/src/capabilities.rs never consults attempts::ROUTES. Its health field is computed from std::fs::metadata alone and its registered field is hard-coded true for every row it emits, so a row can read 'declared' and enabled for a capability no job kind can reach. The surface's own declared_only_note says it is not proof a capability works, but it is silent on whether anything can invoke it.

reachable_by_a_job_note: Attempts::ROUTES yields 11 distinct capabilities from 12 entries. All 11 also appear as keys in the transport's ROUTES dict, and their media-type sets agree with attempts::ROUTE_MEDIA_TYPES (attempts.rs:85-145). Job reachability is conditional on the launch registering the corresponding route for the ten non-text capabilities: the capability is reachable by a job kind once its route is registered, and attempts::claim refuses a disabled capability inside the claim transaction (attempts.rs:271-276).

registered_but_not_job_reachable.how_it_is_reached_instead: A dedicated Core HTTP route, not a job. POST /api/v1/machine/answers (mounted at crates/archeaxis-api/src/runtime/mod.rs:48, handler machine_answer at :494-568) reads a knowledge item's own body as the context and calls Executor::machine_answer (crates/archeaxis-application/src/executor.rs:133-199), which resolves worker_for('machine.answer') and runs services/python-workers/machine/worker_machine_answer.py as a separate process with --question and --max-tokens and parses JSON from its stdout. The retest route POST /api/v1/machine/retests (runtime/mod.rs:58, handler run_retest at :316) reaches the same worker through the same call.

registered_but_not_job_reachable.is_it_actually_registered_in_a_productio: No, not by default. Registration requires a launch document declaring {capability, script}. The staged runtime's worker-profile.json is generated from scripts/release/stage_backend_runtime.py:49-60, whose ROUTE_SCRIPTS table lists 10 capabilities and omits machine.answer; apps/ArcheAxis.Desktop/CoreSupervisor.cs:92-93 declares no routes at all. So in those launches the capability surface does not list machine.answer, and POST /api/v1/machine/answers answers 503 with 'no worker is registered for machine.answer'. It is registered only in a launch that declares it, which today means the two test contracts and the probe script.
registered_but_not_job_reachable.why_a_job_cannot_reach_it: Two independent reasons, both recorded in the sources rather than inferred: the job request schema requires an empty parameters object, so a question cannot be carried in a job request; and the worker's output is an answer plus a loss receipt, not projected text with canonical line anchors, so the text-projection finish path in attempts::finish (attempts.rs:384-467) does not describe it.

advertised_but_unreachable_scope: The two sources this audit was asked to treat as 'advertised': KNOWN_WORKER_IDENTITIES (crates/archeaxis-application/src/executor.rs:521-539) and the transport ROUTES dict (services/python-workers/transport/text_ndjson.py:194-334), read as a set of capability names.

advertised_but_unreachable_how_ruled_out.method: Enumerated every capability name in both sources and tested each one against both reaching paths: (a) a job kind in attempts::ROUTES mapping to it, and (b) a non-job caller in the Core that resolves a worker for it.
advertised_but_unreachable_how_ruled_out.arithmetic: KNOWN_WORKER_IDENTITIES names 12 worker processes; 11 correspond one-to-one with the 11 job-reachable capabilities and the 12th is python-worker-machine-answer-ndjson, whose capability is machine.answer. The transport ROUTES dict has 11 keys, all 11 of them job-reachable. The union is 12 capabilities.
advertised_but_unreachable_how_ruled_out.result: 11 are reached by a job; 1 (machine.answer) is reached by POST /api/v1/machine/answers and POST /api/v1/machine/retests, both of which call Executor::machine_answer, which resolves and runs the worker. No capability in the union is reached by nothing, so the list is empty - not because it was not looked for, but because each name resolves to a named caller.
advertised_but_unreachable_how_ruled_out.the_one_caveat_a_reader_must_keep: machine.answer's reaching path only exists when a launch has registered that route, and no shipped launch does. In a staged-runtime or desktop launch it is therefore not merely un-job-reachable, it is unregistered, and its two HTTP routes answer 503 'no worker is registered for machine.answer'. That is a registration gap, not a 'nothing reaches it' gap: the reaching code path exists and is exercised by the test contracts.

adjacent_case_that_is_out_of_this_scope_.why_adjacent: It is advertised by the standard the repository's own checker uses (it declares ENGINE and def extract) and it is recorded in WORKER-REACHABILITY.json as unrouted. It is NOT advertised in either of the two sources this audit was scoped to: it appears in neither KNOWN_WORKER_IDENTITIES nor the transport ROUTES dict. It also declares no WORKER_IDENTITY, so the Core's identity gate at executor.rs:650-654 would refuse it with 'unexpected worker identity' even if a route named it. If a reader wants a capability that nothing reaches, this is the closest case in the repository - and the correct statement is that it is unrouted on purpose, for three recorded structural reasons, and additionally outside the Core's identity allow-list.
Declares an ENGINE but no WORKER_IDENTITY; the reachability record classifies it as not a capability worker (a network fetch client). Same status: not advertised in the two scoped sources.

how_a_reader_can_tell: READ attempts::ROUTES, not the capability surface. That table is the only production gate for job dispatch (attempts::claim, attempts.rs:250-302, refuses an undeclared kind at :264-267). A capability absent from it cannot be reached by any job, whatever /api/v1/capabilities reports.

DO NOT read health as reachability. crates/archeaxis-api/src/capabilities.rs computes health from std::fs::metadata on two paths (capabilities.rs:34-38 and 68-78) and sets registered: true unconditionally (capabilities.rs:98) for every row it emits. A row exists only for a route the launch declared, so a 'declared' + enabled row means 'this launch declared this route and both files exist' - it says nothing about whether a job kind selects it.

A NAME IN KNOWN_WORKER_IDENTITIES IS NOT A ROUTE. executor.rs:535-538 says so in the source: the list says which identities are recognised at all; the capability registry answers whether a job route drives it.

THE TRANSPORT TABLE IS THE THIRD OPINION. services/python-workers/transport/text_ndjson.py:520 rejects a request whose capability is not a key of its ROUTES dict with 'unsupported capability', and serve_stdio (:624-629) additionally requires the worker to have advertised that capability. A capability in attempts::ROUTES but absent from this dict would fail at the worker instead of at the Core; today the two sets are identical.

THE REPOSITORY'S OWN CHECKER COVERS LESS THAN IT LOOKS LIKE. scripts/check_worker_reachability.py compares worker files against the transport's "worker" paths only (check() at :70-106). It exits 0 while never comparing the transport table against attempts::ROUTES, so passed=true is not evidence that a job can reach every routed capability.

ASK THE LAUNCH, NOT THE CHECKOUT. Whether a route is registered depends on the launch document (launch.rs:30-45), and the only production writers are scripts/release/stage_backend_runtime.py (ROUTE_SCRIPTS, :49-60) and apps/ArcheAxis.Desktop/CoreSupervisor.cs (:92-93, which declares no routes).
conclusion: A job can reach exactly eleven capabilities, and the list is the one attempts::ROUTES declares: text.extract, pdf.extract, image.ocr, archive.inventory, media.probe, media.transcribe, office.structure, canvas.structure, subtitles.structure, html.structure and image.caption. One further capability is registered but no job can reach it: machine.answer, whose worker exists, whose identity python-worker-machine-answer-ndjson is in KNOWN_WORKER_IDENTITIES, and which is absent from attempts::ROUTES on purpose - the transport cannot carry the question it needs, because a job request requires an empty parameters object, and its output is an answer with a loss receipt rather than projected text with canonical anchors. It is reached instead by the Core's own HTTP routes POST /api/v1/machine/answers and POST /api/v1/machine/retests, which call Executor::machine_answer and run the worker as a process. Nothing in either of the two audited sources is reached by nothing at all, so that list is empty: every name resolves to a named caller. The honesty defect a reader should carry away is not that a capability is entirely orphaned, but that the capability surface cannot express the difference: capabilities.rs reports only whether a launch declared a route and whether the worker and interpreter files exist, never whether a job kind can select it, so 'registered and healthy' is compatible with 'no job can run this'. Two caveats keep this honest. First, the registerable set is not the same as the registered set: the ten non-text routes are registered only when a launch declares them, and the staged runtime ships ten of them (stage_backend_runtime.py ROUTE_SCRIPTS) while the desktop host declares none, so machine.answer is not even registered in those launches and its HTTP routes answer 503 'no worker is registered for machine.answer' - the reaching code path exists but no shipped launch wires it. Second, the closest thing in this repository to a capability that nothing reaches is services/python-workers/media/worker_video.py, which is unrouted for three recorded structural reasons and is additionally outside the Core's identity allow-list because it declares no WORKER_IDENTITY; it is not in either of the two sources this audit was scoped to, so it is reported here as an adjacent finding rather than as a hit against the scoped question.
